A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Cost-aware Stopping for Bayesian Optimization, with the same authors and core method. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-process simulations and Bayesian optimization experiments on LCBench and NATS-Bench, including runtime and stopping-behavior analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation and benchmark results and reports additional comparisons, including budgeted acquisition performance and NATS-Bench cost-sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The posterior-update PBGI/LogEIPC stopping criterion and its acquisition functions remain unchanged. Both unknown-cost formulations were already described in v1; v2 selects the existing expected-cost formulation for evaluation rather than introducing a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Adult replaces Volkert in the reported LCBench evaluations, changing coverage from Volkert's 10-class classification problem to Adult's binary income-classification problem. Adult's dimensions were listed in v1, but its evaluation results were absent. Fashion-MNIST, Higgs, the three NATS-Bench datasets, and the 1D/8D synthetic tasks remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds Immediate across the main comparisons and includes PRB in 8D regret experiments, where v1 explicitly omitted it despite measuring its runtime separately. New Figure 11 evaluates PBGI-D, previously only discussed. The unknown-cost comparison also replaces LogEIPC-inv with LogEIPC-exp.

E3.justification: The main NATS comparison changes cost weight from 1e-4 to 1e-5, with additional sweeps reaching 1e-6. v2 selects LogEIPC-exp for unknown costs and adds a budgeted evaluation with 10,000 seconds after initialization. Its PRB thresholds match v1's appendix, resolving conflicting main-text reporting rather than establishing retuning. New NATS trajectories extend beyond the stated 200-iteration cap, leaving their precise horizon unclear.

E4.justification: v2 adds an acquisition-only budgeted comparison to examine the source of performance differences and NATS cost-sensitivity analyses revealing late stopping on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet16-120. It removes v1 Figure 16's NATS proxy-versus-actual-runtime analysis. The runtime comparison, posterior-update case study, and LCBench cost-mismatch analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 50 random seeds and report means with error bars equal to twice the standard error. No new repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes substantially: SRGap-med failures change from 47 to 0 on Fashion-MNIST and 50 to 31 on Higgs; PBGI failures on CIFAR-100 change from 0 to 3. Results are added for Immediate, 8D PRB, budgeted acquisition comparisons, Adult, and NATS cost sweeps, while Volkert and NATS runtime-mismatch results disappear. Changed NATS cost weights preclude interpreting the main plots as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v1 Theorem 1 bounds cumulative cost; v2 Theorem 2 states a stronger bound on cost-adjusted simple regret relative to Immediate. Lemma 1 extracts an argument already used in v1's proof, and Corollary 3 formalizes the previously discussed budget-scaling implication. However, v2's theorem proof still concludes with the old cumulative-cost bound rather than explicitly completing the strengthened inequality.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion redefine the main theoretical contribution around a cost-adjusted-regret guarantee rather than a cumulative-cost guarantee. The abstract and contribution list also narrow the empirical claim from consistently matching or outperforming alternatives to usually doing so.

C2.justification: v2 refines the existing model-mismatch discussion with late-stopping failures on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet16-120 at cost weight 1e-5, and worse-than-Immediate performance on Adult under unknown costs. It also explains why equality with Immediate can be unavoidable when costs are high and clarifies the problem-specified interpretation of cost conversion.

D1.justification: v1's first-page code-access link is removed without replacement. v2 adds the budgeted experiment's choices U = 50 and B - C = 10,000 seconds and explains selecting the first three LCBench-lite datasets. Most implementation details, including BoTorch, CPU execution, initialization, and GP fitting, remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Foumani and Bostanabad (2025) on multi-fidelity stopping and Hu et al. (2025) in the theoretical extension discussion. It qualifies the earlier categorical description of prior stopping research and repositions its theoretical novelty around cost-adjusted regret. The remaining cited literature is retained.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the theory, budget-scaling, practical-guidance, and empirical discussion sections. Unknown-cost alternatives move largely into the appendix, and a new LLM-usage disclosure shifts appendix lettering. Citation style and headings change, but most introductory, methodological, and experimental-setup prose remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The document template and figure placement change throughout. v1's separate LCBench and NATS main figures merge into v2 Figure 4; Immediate reference lines and uncertainty bands alter several displays. New budgeted and NATS trajectory figures, revised legends and axes, and removal of the NATS runtime-mismatch figure substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Adding Immediate and 8D PRB comparisons and NATS cost-sensitivity plots strengthens evaluation and exposes failures that appropriately qualify v1's broad performance claim. These gains are limited by removal of the code link and NATS runtime-mismatch evidence, plus theoretical presentation problems: Section 3.1 claims strict improvement despite a non-strict bound, and the revised proof still ends at the older cost-only conclusion.
